title: A Colorful Sting
description: Parasitic wasps like the Torymus calcaratus depend on other insects to complete their life cycle. With a long, needle-like organ called an ovipositor (bottom right), they inject their eggs into the larvae of a host species. At the Stuttgart State Museum of Natural History’s entomology collection, photographer Thorben Danke took 289 shots of the symbiotic predator and combined them using a stacking technique to create this sharp, vibrant image. This photo is featured in the "In Focus" series in the September 2026 issue of National Geographic.
translated_description: 像Torymus calcaratus这样的寄生蜂依赖其他昆虫来完成其生命周期。它们借助一种细长如针的器官——产卵器（右下角），将卵注入寄主物种的幼虫体内。在斯图加特国家自然历史博物馆的昆虫学藏品中，摄影师托尔本·丹克拍摄了这种共生捕食者的289张照片，并通过堆叠技术将其合成，创作出这幅清晰而生动的图像。这张照片刊登在《国家地理》2026年9月刊的“焦点”系列中。
